finding: 36.1% of women with CFS reported endometriosis; those with EM had more pelvic pain (OR 9.0) and hysterectomy (OR 10.3) than CFS-only.
note: secondary analysis, tiny n, no controls

finding: US ambulatory data 2000-2009: ME/CFS visits stable, 71% had comorbidities (depression 36%).
Psoriasis was associated with later CFS diagnosis (adjusted HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.07-2.06), attenuated by phototherapy or immunomodulators.
Systematic review rates methodological quality of CBT and GET RCTs as low, with bias affecting subjective primary outcomes.
Opinion piece arguing ME, CFS and chronic fatigue are distinct entities and that CBT/GET are ineffective.
Accelerometer data: children with mild-moderate CFS/ME did less than half recommended activity; three latent activity classes.
Antibodies to neuronal proteins were not more frequent in ME/CFS (specific antibodies in 1 patient vs 2 controls); seropositivity linked to shorter duration and more severity.
EBV dUTPase altered expression of BBB and synaptic genes in human astrocytes, microglia and endothelial cells.
Patch-clamp in a new cohort confirmed impaired TRPM3 activity in patients' NK cells.
Historical comparison of ME/CFS and HIV/AIDS research and care.
Routine labs mostly normal, but serum creatine kinase was lower in severe ME/CFS (median 54 vs 101.5 U/L in controls; OR 0.05 vs controls).
Adolescents with CFS scored higher on depression subscales than healthy and asthma controls.
Requirement of substantial functional reduction is redundant for stringent case definitions.
In the chronic stress rat model, proprioceptor hyperactivation and spinal microglia accompanied long-lasting pain.
Computational model of endocrine-immune signalling constrained to exercise-challenge cytokine data predicts overexpression of CRH, CXCL8, estrogen, FSH and LH at rest.
Life-story interviews show stigmatisation and lack of legitimacy in contested illnesses.

n: 42 patients vs 9 controls (15 patients combined network)
finding: Network analysis of autonomic, cortisol and cytokine measures found patients' autonomic network split into two modules (blood pressure and stroke volume dominated).
Systematic review of ME/CFS epigenetic studies plus transposable-element screening proposes endogenous transposon activation driving innate immune activation.
Family carers report identity and relationship disruption and distress from scepticism.
CD57 expression on T cells was lower in CFS (percent 7.5 vs 13.3, p=0.024; per-cell 331 vs 1003, p<=0.0001).
note: small, single centre, n not given

finding: After CBT, shorter illness duration, lower baseline fatigue and lower frustration predicted better long-term outcome (up to 10 years).
Database review of commonly prescribed drugs that may alter candidate miRNA biomarkers in FM and ME/CFS.
Timed loaded standing endurance correlated with SF-36 physical functioning only, among self-report and test pairs.
Adolescents with CFS scored higher on unhelpful cognitive and behavioural responses to symptoms, which predicted later fatigue.
Work rate at ventilatory threshold fell more from day 1 to day 2 of CPET in ME/CFS (6.3-9.8% decrease proposed cut-off).
Authors defend PACE trial conclusions against Wilshire reanalysis.
Uncontrolled stepped-care CBT in community mental health improved fatigue and function with sustained gains, but less than specialist centre outcomes.
Commentary: most single-agent drug trials in ME/CFS inconclusive; proposes combination, systems-level approaches.
NMR plasma metabolite profiles separated depression from fatigue groups with CNN and PLS-DA.
Only 69 of 1400 fatigued Poles met Fukuda criteria; 50% had orthostatic intolerance symptoms and 62% daytime sleepiness.
Gene-module analysis of expression data found small effects in immune regulation and mitochondrial modules, with sex differences; used to suggest repurposed drugs.
note: small, exploratory, drug repositioning in silico

finding: Thematic analysis of patient reports of dismissive physician encounters.
Patient-driven PEM survey identified domains (triggers, onset, duration) that existing PEM questionnaires miss.
Adolescents with CFS did not consistently show higher perfectionism or unhelpful beliefs about emotions; neither predicted later fatigue.

n: UK 89 moderate + 29 severe; South Africa 143 moderate
finding: No pathogenic mtDNA mutations; patients in both cohorts had excess of individuals lacking a mildly deleterious population mtDNA variant.
note: control comparison details not in abstract

finding: Australian surveillance: incidence 0.25/100,000 in ages 4-9; marked regional variation in 10-17 (Victoria 17.5/100,000); most cases female, post-infectious.
IBD was associated with higher later risk of CFS diagnosis (adjusted HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.70-2.99).
Follow-up mean 8 years: 38% reported recovery by 5 years and 68% by 10 years; mean illness duration 5 years among those recovered.
Commentary argues ME/CFS and fibromyalgia are distinct illnesses.
Adolescents with ME/CFS had markedly worse quality of life than controls; orthostatic intolerance in 96%; 85% met IOM criteria.
Adolescents with CFS differed from other chronic illness groups on illness perception dimensions.
Ethics argument against classifying ME/CFS as a mental health disorder in UK guideline.
Survey: 64% reported infection around onset; 47% unable to work; 59% fluctuating course, 4% steadily improving.
Cognitive deficits in psychomotor speed persisted in CFS without depression (digit-symbol p=0.004) and correlated with heart rate variability.
FM/CFS more common with silicone breast implants than systemic sclerosis controls (20% vs 2.2%) but not SLE controls.
Fear-avoidance beliefs predicted later fatigue and social adjustment in young people with severe CFS/ME; questionnaires only.
Primary care primer on initiating care.
Commentary: paediatric prevalence estimates (0-3%) vary widely and misdiagnosis likely inflates them.
Submaximal exercise did not change TBARS oxidative stress in ME/CFS; oxidative stress was associated with pain; vagal change partly explained oxidative change in controls only.
59% had visited an ED; one third of ED presentations consistent with orthostatic intolerance; 42% dismissed as psychosomatic.
Focus groups on research priorities and stigma among biobank participants.
Claims data: diagnosis frequency 519-1038 per 100,000, female relative risk 1.2, 35-40% of diagnosed are men; costs 50% above lupus/MS.
CRF patients had higher hs-CRP and lower HRV than CFS; frontal EEG delta/theta/alpha power related to fatigue in CFS.
Repeated forced swimming in mice lowered muscle PDH activity; PDH activator dichloroacetate reduced fatigue-like behaviour.
Thesis: B cell phenotype differences and metabolic profiling of activated B cells in ME/CFS vs controls (details truncated).
PBMC RNA-seq: 27 transcripts up (IL8, NFKBIA, TNFAIP3) and 6 down; IL8 and NFKBIA validated by qPCR.
Among 163 post-trauma BPPV patients, 63% fulfilled Fukuda criteria; speculative link between vestibular disease and ME/CFS.
Patients had higher pain, anxiety and depression and lower QoL than controls; pain related to lower QoL within patients.
Changes in pressure pain thresholds after exercise were associated with changes in complement C4a in ME/CFS but not with elastase.
Psychiatric referral associated with perceived stigma and estrangement, moderated by country.

n: 52 MI patients; CFS n not shown
finding: Thesis on herpesvirus-specific interferon-gamma T cell responses in MI and CFS; abstract truncated.
Swedish agency systematic review of treatment, prognosis and care experiences (abstract minimal).
Systematic review: gut microbiome differences reported in every study but only three significant and findings inconsistent; study quality poor.
Opinion contrasting original ME with International Consensus Criteria.
Uncontrolled 4-day CBT/mindfulness programme: 80% showed self-reported clinical change sustained at 1 year.
Pooled peak VO2 5.2 ml/kg/min lower (95% CI 3.8-6.6) in CFS/ME than healthy controls; high heterogeneity.
Hypothesis review linking raised intracranial pressure to FM, CFS and IIH.
Interviews: patients define recovery as living without fear of relapse and are sceptical complete recovery is possible.
Burn injury associated with later CFS diagnosis (adjusted HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.41-1.56).
All described fluctuation and symptom increase after activity (payback), varying in activity amount needed.
UK ME/CFS Biobank: ME/CFS scored lower than MS and controls on almost all SF-36 domains, and had lower employment and income.
Mast cell progenitors showed no differences in maturity or CD154 versus others; HLA-DR+/CD154- lower in CFS/ME than systemic mastocytosis.
Rituximab serum levels did not differ between responders and non-responders; no anti-drug antibodies.

n: 272 ME/CFS vs 136 HC vs 76 MS vs 37 CF
finding: Hand grip strength was markedly lower in ME/CFS, especially severe (minimum grip 15.3 kg lower than healthy controls).
About a quarter (155/627) of ME/CFS patients met POTS criteria on tilt; abbreviated 2-5 min tilt would miss many (median time to criteria about 3 min).
Spilanthes extract reduced oxidative stress markers in a water-immersion stress mouse model.
Dual-isotope blood volume averaged 11 ml/kg below reference; lower in those with orthostatic intolerance (56 vs 66 ml/kg).
Selenium-polysaccharide from green tea altered BUN, corticosterone and urine metabolites in a rat stress model of CFS.
DKI/NODDI diffusion MRI showed lower FA in corpus callosum genu and right internal capsule and right superior longitudinal fasciculus abnormalities.
Low omega-3 index (mean 5.75%) in 92.6% of patients; no association with fatigue or sleep scores.
Whole-blood immune gene sets split CFS into subgroups; lower plasma norepinephrine was associated with higher fatigue.
Parental fatigue and distress were not correlated with adolescent fatigue.
Describes development and psychometrics of the DePaul Symptom Questionnaire.
Self-reported CFS had lower physical activity and longer sleep than controls; both extremes linked to higher symptom severity.
Adolescents with CFS had equivalent fatigue to fatigued MS but normal neurocognitive testing.
Review of Japanese PET and MRI work: reduced cerebral blood flow and glucose use, reduced serotonin transporter density, and widespread neuroinflammation on TSPO PET.
Commentary on mast cell and microglia stress-inflammation with a luteolin product.
Feedback on failed performance validity test improved subsequent reaction time in CFS.
Development of the DePaul Post-Exertional Malaise Questionnaire with preliminary validation.
CD24+ B cells were more frequent in patients and CD24 expression related to AMPK phosphorylation and B cell maturation in vitro.
Defines minimal clinically important difference of SF-36 physical function for children with CFS/ME.
Interviews in GES trial: deteriorated group described symptom exacerbation after guided graded exercise self-help.
Adolescents with CFS had poorer school attendance, participation and academic performance.
Withdrawn Cochrane review of Chinese herbal medicine RCTs for chronic fatigue.
14-day diary: daily energy, sleep and need satisfaction fluctuated and were reciprocally related.
CFS label raised intended social support from friends in a student vignette experiment.

n: 25 vs 25 Canadian, 25 Norwegian cases, 6 US controls
finding: Peptide microarray immunosignature of 256 peptides separated ME/CFS from controls across cohorts.
Opinion proposing stratifying CFS/fibromyalgia into immune-mediated entities.
Pilot community study: 22% of respondents did not meet Fukuda or Canadian criteria; severely affected want to take part in research but have high symptom burden.
School nurse role in supporting students with ME/CFS.
Five DSQ PEM duration items classified 81.7% of ME/CFS correctly and misclassified 16.6% of MS and post-polio patients.
Oral microbiome composition differed in CFS (more Fusobacteria, Leptotrichia, Prevotella; less Veillonella, Porphyromonas); diversity unchanged.
Proposes an operational definition of ME centred on muscle fatigability.
Confirmatory factor analysis of ME/CFS stigma scale; high stigma endorsed.
Protocol for systematic review of ME/CFS prevalence in Europe.
Review: evidence for probiotics in CFS/ME poor and limited, in contrast to IBS.
CFS without depression was not more likely to show illusory mental health than controls, arguing against reducing CFS to somatisation.
Resting HRV was lower in CFS before warm water immersion (63 vs 73, p=0.04) and heart rate higher after (86 vs 78).
In a prospective dichloroacetate trial, six pre-treatment characteristics predicted responders (AUC 0.92).
Adolescents used official then peer-led online resources for coping.
Very long lncRNAs NTT, MIAT and EmX2OS were higher in PBMC of ME/CFS; NTT and EmX2OS rose with severity.
ME/CFS had slower maximum reading speed and poorer crowded visual acuity, correlated with each other.
Home-based CBT rehabilitation: all six returned to school/college by 12 months.
Patch-clamp showed reduced TRPM3 current amplitude in NK cells from CFS/ME patients.
Quiet standing sway showed poorer postural control in CFS and FM; a cognitive task did not change it.
SF-36 cutoffs (e.g. physical functioning at or below 80) discriminate young adults with CFS/ME.
Emotional regulation impairment was found only in CFS with higher depression; somatisation supported in some.
Plasma TNF-alpha showed a non-significant rise in CFS/ME (p=0.056); cytokines correlated with psychiatric symptoms.
Review proposing molecular physiotherapy to study manual therapy responses.
Dry eye syndrome was associated with later CFS diagnosis (adjusted HR about 1.61).
Non-depressed patients with suicidal ideation described feeling trapped and loss of self and stigma.
T1 spin-echo MRI showed lower signal in a brainstem region and higher signal in sensorimotor white matter (P_FWE=0.002); no volume differences.
Hypothesis that glymphatic dysfunction explains some CFS and that CSF diversion may help.
Meta-analysis: PEM was 10.4 times more likely to be associated with ME/CFS than control status.
Latent class analysis found six symptom subtypes (including orthostatic intolerance and gastrointestinal) with different SF-36 functioning.
History and discourse analysis rejecting the claim that ME/CFS patient groups are militant.
Intracranial compliance and resting cerebral perfusion did not differ from controls; lower compliance and higher perfusion tracked orthostatic symptoms within patients.
Review of muscle abnormalities in CFS (oxidative damage, fibre shift to fast phenotype, mitochondrial dysfunction).
Systematic review of physiotherapy RCTs found no clearly superior approach; four studies only.
64% of CFS patients met DSM personality disorder criteria in a Spanish clinic sample.
Edible fungus extract improved exercise tolerance and antioxidant markers in mouse CFS models.
CFS had reduced LPS-induced IL-6 and TNF-alpha and reduced dex suppression of TNF; cortisol before and after dex did not differ from controls.
Sociological analysis of CFS/ME as a biopolitical object.
Actigraphy showed lower activity, relative amplitude and activity rhythm stability and lower nocturnal distal skin temperature in CFS/ME; no sleep latency differences.
Abnormal range of motion fell from 78% to 20% over 2 years alongside multimodal therapy.
Electroacupuncture raised grip force and muscle PGC-1alpha in a rat stress model.
Structural MRI regional volumes classified CFS vs controls at 79.6% accuracy, below self-report (96%).
Lower cortisol awakening response in CFS (4.2 vs 6.1 nmol/L, p=0.036); hair cortisol trend lower (p=0.062); anakinra for 4 weeks slightly lowered hair cortisol versus placebo.
Critique of the Dutch Health Council report's diagnostic criteria.
Poor sleep quality was linked to pain, psychopathology, fibromyalgia and severe autonomic dysfunction.
Lower Tregs, higher NKT-like cells, lower NKG2C and higher NK CD69/CD56bright in patients; classification model reached 70% accuracy.
Metformin and compound 991 activated AMPK and raised glucose uptake in ME/CFS myotubes; ATP content lower in ME/CFS cultures.
CFS scored no higher than controls on Autism-Spectrum Quotient.
Systematic review: subjective cognitive complaints exceed objective deficits; slow processing and attention deficits reported.
Unsupportive social interactions and stigma associated with depression and suicidal ideation; 7.1% had ideation without depression.
Probiotic RCTs in CFS: L. casei Shirota reduced anxiety; B. infantis lowered inflammatory markers; evidence limited.
DNA methylation plus symptom scores define four ME/CFS subtypes (1939 CpGs), differing in immune gene methylation and PEM.
Stroop fMRI: CFS had longer response times and lower BOLD sample entropy in ten regions; activation maps did not differ between groups.
Weighted standing time stratified severity; only serum activin B differed from controls, with no differences in other cytokines or serum/urine markers.
After one sitting isometric yoga session, fatigue fell and vagal activity increased with changes in blood markers.
21% of hypersomnolence patients met SEID criteria.
CFS and FM had larger postural sway and lower control frequencies than controls.
Interviews describe disrupted occupational and peer life and gradual acceptance.
Urine LC-MS: creatine, indoleacetaldehyde, phytosphingosine and pyroglutamate lower in CFS students; arginine-proline pathway disordered.
In vitro rituximab lowered NK cell lysis and raised degranulation in CFS/ME NK cells.
Orthostatic intolerance symptoms in 91%; disequilibrium on standing in 32.5% of those with OI and hemodynamic dysfunction in 47.5%.
Serum extracellular vesicle fraction was higher (p=0.007) and vesicles smaller (p=0.014) in CFS/ME.
Global cerebral blood flow was normal at rest and during PASAT; regional CBF related to fatigue recovery differed.
SEID-positive adolescents differed only in mood score; no differences in cardiovascular, inflammatory, neuroendocrine variables after multiple comparison correction.
Cognitive-behavioural model was generally not supported, especially under stricter case definitions.
Nocturnal low-frequency HRV was higher in CFS across sleep stages, suggesting higher sympathetic and lower parasympathetic tone in sleep.
During a grip-effort task, CFS invested less effort after feedback at high effort, with reduced prefrontal feedback activity, proportional to fatigue and beliefs.
Cardiac structure and exercise capacity were similar; cytokine profile 18 h after submaximal exercise discriminated patients (kappa 0.62; CD40L, IL-1beta, IFN-alpha, CXCL1).

n: 38 Dutch vs 52 UK CFS vs 51 HC
finding: CFS groups showed attentional and interpretation bias toward somatic information in both countries.
Gut eukaryote (18S) diversity was not significantly different in ME/CFS; no taxa linked to disease.
Contrast sensitivity was reduced at low spatial frequencies with narrower bandwidth in ME.
Over 18 months, NK cell and naive T cell proportions were modestly related to physical functioning and symptom counts.
Patients reported more dyspnea only during recovery after rebreathing; physiological reactivity was not different.
Default mode network showed weaker connectivity (mPFC to parietal) and more complex PCC BOLD signal in CFS.
Japanese review hypothesising autoimmune neuroinflammation, citing rituximab benefit from open-label work.
Japanese diagnostic criteria and treatment overview.
Review of Japanese TSPO PET showing widespread neuroinflammation related to symptom severity.
Japanese history review referencing TSPO PET evidence of microglial activation.

population: severe housebound ME/CFS vs household controls
finding: Thesis: NGS and NMR of gut, faecal and serum microbiome in severe ME/CFS with household controls (results truncated).
Critique of Dutch Health Council report as unbalanced about somatic evidence.
Japanese review plus comprehensive blood metabolomics aimed at a diagnostic biomarker (details not in abstract).
Individual patient data review of exercise therapy for CFS (no abstract available).
0.9% (163) of middle-school students met the CFS definition, more in males and older students.
Posturography composite balance score was lower in CFS (69.0 vs 78.8) and related to physical function; vestibular impairment only in CFS with FM.
School functioning is mostly measured only as attendance, with inconsistent instruments.
No group differences in cerebral blood flow (Doppler) or HRV responses to physical or emotional stress.
Plasma BNP higher in CFS (p=0.013), associated with smaller end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes on cardiac MRI; unrelated to disease duration.
Overexertion was most harmful to function in those with higher available energy, consistent with energy envelope theory.
Plasma TGF-beta isoforms compared with controls and neuroendocrine/clinical markers (result not in visible abstract).
Physician interviews identify challenges in defining and measuring recovery.
Most cardiological parameters did not differ, but CFS was associated with low blood pressure; hypotension and orthostatic intolerance proposed as explanation.
NR3C1-1F glucocorticoid receptor gene hypomethylation replicated in CFS (small differences, only one CpG surviving correction).
Morphine's effect on pain thresholds in CFS/FM was comparable to placebo; baseline temporal summation higher and deep tissue pain pressure lower than controls.
Physical signs (tender coeliac plexus, etc.) showed inter-rater agreement and improved identification of CFS/ME; small single-centre study.
CSF miRNAs were similar at rest across groups; after exercise CFS had 12 diminished miRNAs, with patterns distinct from Gulf War Illness.
Serum 25(OH) vitamin D was higher in CFS/ME (60.2 vs 47.3 nmol/L, supplement-related); no deficiency or link to fatigue.
Symptom-based phenotypes replicated; polysymptomatic and pain-only phenotypes had lower odds of improvement at 1 year (MOR 0.43 and 0.33 in UK).
34.6% met major depression and 28.8% an anxiety disorder on structured interview.
Orchid extract improved behavioural and oxidative markers in a forced-swim rat model.
Self-reported autonomic and cognitive symptoms higher in CFS but objective Task Force autonomic measures did not differ from controls.
After physical or cognitive challenge, nocturnal parasympathetic HRV fell and inactivity rose during post-exertional fatigue.
Higher resting TGF-beta in CFS was a spurious assay-batch artefact; no group differences in other cytokines or in exercise responses.
With depression excluded, childhood trauma scores in CFS were not higher than in controls.
VBM: larger grey matter (amygdala, insula) and lower white matter volume (midbrain, pons, right temporal) in CFS.
Lightning Process plus specialist care improved SF-36 physical function by 12.5 points at 6 months versus care alone.
Personal ethics case study about declining an IOM panel invitation.
Actigraphy showed longer sleep latency, time in bed and total sleep time, and later rise time in adolescents with CFS/ME.
Structural model linked depression, higher evening salivary cortisol and inflammation in CFS.
Reduced resting connectivity between right anterior insula and posterior parietal cortex in adolescent CFS.
Systematic review: no study targeted anxiety in children with CFS; evidence insufficient on what treatment to offer.
Patient surveys: CBT helped 8-35%, graded exercise worsened symptoms in 54-74%, pacing most favoured (44-82% benefit).
Cortisol levels normal in both groups but morning-afternoon correlation absent in CFS; total T3 lower in CFS with normal T4 and TSH.
ME/CFS research volunteers held less stigmatising attitudes.
Activity pacing scores were not associated with pain, fatigue or disability.
Polysomnography found treatable sleep disorders in over half (OSA 40%, RLS 41%, PLMD 9%).
Treadmill CFS rat model had higher 5-HT, 5-HIAA and tryptophan than controls, opposite to stress-model rats.
Oxford criteria classed about 20-25% of the US population as CFS versus about 2% on Fukuda; 85% of Oxford cases inappropriately classified.
Childhood sexual harassment predicted fatigue and poor physical functioning.
1-year: 27.5% much better, 20% worse; services varied in therapy.
Home-based CBT self-management dominated usual care economically.
MRI of medial prefrontal cortex correlated with unrefreshing sleep scores; lower MT and T1w intensities in CFS (uncorrected).
Commentary rejecting PACE trial conclusions.
Illness course (fluctuating 60%, constantly worse 16%) associated with symptom and functioning differences.
Hypothesis linking CFS to low-grade intracranial pressure disorders.
Review: CBT studies with objective outcomes show no evidence of improved physical capability or return to work.
Systematic review: dietary modification evidence narrow and inconsistent; some positive signals for D-ribose, omega-3 and polyphenols (animal).
ME/CFS respondents reported more functional limitation and more severe symptoms than MS.
Pain neuroscience education: baseline kinesiophobia and worrying predicted less reduction in catastrophizing.
Review compares D-lactic acidosis symptoms to ME/CFS; only preliminary evidence for D-lactate-producing bacteria in ME/CFS.
Interviews on experiences of NHS specialist services.
Multidisciplinary rehabilitation reduced fatigue more than CBT at 52 weeks but cost more; QALY difference not significant.
Discourse analysis of satirical texts in an online ME community.
Acupuncture lowered T-bet and raised GATA-3 expression in a rat CFS model.
Critique alleging bias in PACE investigators' accounts of CBT/GET literature.
Bioinformatics and primer testing show XMRV PCR primers bind non-specifically to repeats in human DNA, explaining unreliable association.
76% of CFS sample met IOM criteria but 44% met revised London criteria for ME, with greater impairment.
Argues CBT evidence for reducing distress is weak and patient surveys report worsening.
Cognitive coping strategies related to depressive symptoms.
Reviews patient survey data 2001-2015: GET worsens most patients, CBT no change, pacing improves.
Bias appraisal comparing a psychosocial trial (PACE) with a cellular study.
Adolescents with CFS spent longer in bed, had delayed mid-sleep and more variable sleep-wake rhythm, and reported more insomnia and sleepiness.
CFS had lower pressure pain thresholds (about 25% lower than MS) and higher temporal summation, indicating pain facilitation rather than impaired inhibition.
Vitamin E lower in patients (SMD -1.57) but not in high-quality studies; no consistent vitamin or mineral deficiency.
Commentary: PACE outcome changes inflated efficacy claims; no objective improvement.
Cluster analysis found five comorbidity groups (e.g., fibromyalgia, MCS, sicca, hypovitaminosis D, hyperlaxity, endometriosis).
Fewer than half had seen an ME/CFS specialist; 99% wanted specialist care.
Content analysis of US newspaper coverage of CFS.
CSF 51-plex cytokines differed between atypical and classical ME/CFS (lower IL-17A, CXCL9 in atypical); IL-1RA pattern suggests IL-1 signalling disturbance in classical.
Jawbone osteonecrosis tissue from CFS patients showed 30-fold RANTES and 20-fold FGF-2 versus healthy jawbone.
Commentary criticising PACE unblinded design with subjective outcomes.
Patients reported satisfaction and partial improvement with CBT but incomplete recovery.
Up to 10 years after CBT, fatigue and physical functioning had worsened since post-treatment; 37% had normal fatigue and 70% unimpaired function.
Epimedium polysaccharide altered urinary metabolites and two pathways in a rat CFS model.
